name: Abyssal Ghost Manta
desc: A shadow nine metres across, with nothing above it that could account for one and no mass on any instrument aimed at it. Nothing has ever been recovered from under it.

name: Abyssal Irisfin
desc: A thousand eyes open and close in no order and never all at once. Ratings who have gutted one report the pattern continues afterwards, on the inside.

name: Abyssal Gazer
desc: One eye the size of a fist, slotted crosswise like a goat's, in a body that is otherwise unremarkable. It holds a gaze longer than anything without a mind should.

name: Abyssal Necrophyte
desc: Arrives decaying and stops at half, the rot holding where no chemistry aboard will move it. Whatever it was before the abyss had it was dead a long time first.

name: Abyssal Eyestar
desc: Five arms, six pupils, no agreement between them about where the middle is. It keeps its shape while it is watched. The watch is not optional, and every crew learns this once.

name: Abyssal Razorback Shrimp
desc: Segmented far past what its length allows, several of them plainly the same segment twice. It is kept under restraint, and the restraint is inspected daily.

name: Abyssal Razorclam
desc: Opens along three hinges. Reality permits two. Nobody has explained the third, and the survey has stopped asking for an explanation.

name: Abyssal Stoneplate Lobster
desc: Plated in something nearer slag than shell and cold enough to take skin off through a glove. It works its claws for a day after everything else in it has stopped.

name: Abyssal Venomous Aranea
desc: Neither fish nor arachnid and committed to both, with a venom that has beaten three attempts at classification. The cooks and medical agree on how to handle it, for once.

name: Abyssal Yellowback
desc: Very nearly ordinary, which is the whole of the problem - old crews will not have one aboard at any price. The yellow is not pigment, and it does not stay on the animal.

name: Abyssal Nautilus
desc: A chambered shell wound inward, spiralling into itself past the point where there is anywhere left to go. Each chamber holds some of the abyss. None of them drain.

name: Steel Pipechovies
desc: Five or six at a time, each a straight length of dull steel with a mouth at one end. Whatever was being copied was a ration tin, and it was not swimming.

name: Roider Mudfish
desc: A bottom-feeder's build and a bottom-feeder's manner, in a place with neither bottom nor mud. Roider crews rate them highly. This says more about roider crews.

name: Berylcuda
desc: Green-scaled and hard as the mineral it is named for, carrying a barracuda's jaw on a Domain food-stock body. Two patterns through as one, and neither of them finished.

name: Coudplate Tetra
desc: Plated along the back in cloud-shaped scutes, armour against pressures hyperspace has never had. Collectors pay for the ones that came through symmetrical.

name: Tiger Sailfish
desc: Trails a banner longer than its own body, striped to be seen by something that is not on any record. The banner goes on moving after the animal has stopped.

name: Silver Slipstreamer
desc: Silver, and already at speed, holding a heading as though the slipstream it left were still running under it. One of the few that behaves as its shape suggests.

name: Green Bass
desc: Green, blunt, and obliging. A shape with nothing stronger to settle into settles into a bass, and some survey outfits have stopped recording them at all.

name: Jungle Snapper
desc: Small and deep-bodied, marked in reds and greens like something raised under a canopy. The colour is the first thing to go and the last thing anyone remembers.

name: Blue Ochtogon Magifin
desc: Eight fins around a body plated in flat panels, too regular to be chance and lit along every seam. It is not built like an animal and does not move like one.

name: Blue Tang
desc: An untroubled blue that holds longer than most colours manage - the shape appears to suit whatever has assumed it. Reef stock, from reefs centuries under.

name: Soul Bream
desc: Broad, plain, and quiet, and the crews who bring them in will not say how the name came about. Something in a bream reads as occupied rather than alive.

name: Venomous Sailfish
desc: Sail-finned and patterned to warn rather than to hide, which turns out to be honest advertising. A week in the medbay for anyone who tests the claim.

name: Ole' Carp
desc: Grey, slow, and uninterested in resisting anything at all. Every ship of any age has one in the logs and not one crew remembers acquiring it.

name: Credfish
desc: Flat, hard-edged, and stamped along the flank with a figure the eye keeps trying to read as a denomination. Not legal tender in any port. This has stopped nobody.

name: Long Waller
desc: Two metres of whiskered patience, feeling along a riverbed that is not there and never was. Crews find it endearing or unbearable, with no ground in between.

name: Shimmerclam
desc: Shut on arrival and shut since, against every tool rated for the job. The shell runs through colours it carries no pigment for, and that is the whole of its behaviour.

name: Common Crag Crab
desc: Moves sideways, and keeps moving sideways until something stops it. Ten legs, which is the correct number, and no comfort whatsoever.

name: Volturnian Crab
desc: Blue through the shell rather than across it, and the nearest thing hyperspace has produced to true Volturnian stock. Worth rather more than the care it takes.

name: Adolescent Pyrcrab
desc: Low, broad, and slow to commit to anything, which makes it one of the easier ones to have aboard. It runs warm to the touch, and warmer the longer it is held.

name: Adult Pyrcrab
desc: The same animal grown out, and hot enough now to raise blisters through a work glove. Every rating describes a different fault in it, and each is sure the others are wrong.

name: Eelcat
desc: Long, whiskered, and inclined to knot itself around whatever is nearest. The knots do not survive inspection as knots, but no better word has been offered.

name: Egg
desc: Hyperspace does not spawn, so this is a shape with no process behind it. It has never hatched. Standing orders are not to be in the compartment when it does.

name: Bloody Damsel
desc: An orange bright enough to read as a hazard light, and territorial about a territory that does not exist. It squares up to machinery many times its size, every time.

name: Goldfish
desc: Ornamental, inedible, and entirely without fight, turning up on ships whose crews have been thinking about home. Half the Sector calls it luck. The other half calls it a wasted berth.

name: Bluefin Theta
desc: Rises for air in a medium that has none, over and over, at the surface of nothing at all. The blue along the fin is the only part of it that ever holds still.

name: Abyssal Rockfish
desc: Squat and heavily spined, green along the belly with something that is not algae and does not wash off. The name records where it was found, as a warning.

name: Adolescent Razorspine
desc: Thin as a blade and lit along the underside, a depth-trick from depths hyperspace has never had. The lights go out one at a time, in an order nobody has worked out.

name: Silver Razorspine
desc: The same pattern grown out and gone metallic, heavy enough to deform gear rated well above it. Whatever it copied, it took some of the ship along with it.

name: Lunacyte
desc: Pale and unhurried, lit from within on a cycle that matches nothing aboard. Named by a crew that watched one for a full shift, and would not afterwards explain the name.

name: Poison Jelly
desc: Trails filaments far longer than the bell could support, and goes on trailing them after the bell has stopped. It stings for hours, and longer than that in the memory.

name: Aetherial Jelly
desc: Barely present and barely holding, a shape more suggested than built. Handled roughly it comes apart, and the pieces do not stay pieces for long.

name: Mossy Bass
desc: Furred green along the back with something that is not moss, in a place with nothing for moss to hold to. It fights hard, briefly, and then not at all.

name: Largemouth Bass
desc: Big, blunt, obliging, and the most logged specimen in the Sector by a wide margin. Two together are never the same size, and never wrong in the same direction twice.

name: Larva
desc: A thing stopped between shapes, and allowed to stand on the grounds that larvae are permitted to be unfinished. It is the only ruling anyone has got out of the phenomenon.

name: Waterpillar
desc: Segmented and ringed, moving in a wave with nothing available to push against. A land pattern, and nobody has explained where it was encountered.

name: Emmerling
desc: Named by the crew that recorded the first, and the name held for want of a competing suggestion. No template has been found for it, in Domain records or since.

name: Volturnian Lobster
desc: Blue-shelled and heavy through the claw, near enough the true Askonian article to fetch the true price. Near enough is doing the work, and the trade knows it.

name: Rock Lobster
desc: Grey, unremarkable, and gripping whatever is nearest rather than the reverse. Good eating by the standards available out here, which are not standards so much as hopes.

name: Striped Mackerel
desc: Barred, quick, and schooling with nothing to school alongside. The bars keep moving after the animal has stopped, which is where most crews stop watching.

name: Marlin
desc: Long bill, long body, and a run that costs equipment. Bringing one in is generally the end of the work for that watch, one way or the other.

name: Mussel
desc: Clamped shut around a rock that did not come through with it. Whatever it believes it is holding is not aboard, and the grip has never once slackened.

name: Deep Terror
desc: Eight arms, deep red, and a great deal better coordinated than the crew watching it. It gets into things, and it has never once been found where it was left.

name: Yellow King
desc: Holds the deck as a court rather than a berth, and the yellow of it is the same yellow every time. Crews who stand a long watch over one begin deferring to it.

name: Pacu Pacu
desc: Blunt, flat-toothed, and disconcertingly human about the mouth. The teeth are the part that came through cleanest, which is not the part anyone would have chosen.

name: Perch
desc: Striped, spiny, and ordinary in every respect that can be measured. Most watches, that is a relief.

name: Pomfret
desc: Silver and deep-bodied, holding its shape better than most, which makes it a common first specimen. It is also the one crews are least able to describe afterwards.

name: Hyperprawn
desc: Translucent, thumb-length, and arriving by the hundred. One is nothing worth logging; several hundred turning together in the same instant is in the logs for a reason.

name: Pufferfish
desc: Arrives slack and unimpressive, having concluded that the danger has passed. It has not.

name: Ballooner
desc: A pufferfish with its mind made up - inflated, spined, and declining to come back down. Reality permits the volume and is plainly unhappy about the source.

name: Deepwater Pufferfish
desc: Blue, spined, and already inflated on the way through, as though something down there had startled it. Nothing had, according to everything that was watching.

name: Silver Star
desc: Winged, silver, gliding on a medium with nothing to glide upon. It matches no record in any Domain database, and xeno-survey has declined to take an interest.

name: Gargantuan Waller
desc: A waller grown past all sense, heavy-headed and wrong about its own proportions. It reads as a catfish until somebody measures it, and then it takes a winch.

name: Nemo
desc: Banded orange and white and sealed in a bag of water nobody aboard put it in. The bag came through with it, holds pressure, and reads as standard plasteel on analysis.

name: Curious Damsel
desc: Small, bright, and inclined to follow machinery rather than flee it. Curiosity is not on the list of things these are supposed to be capable of.

name: Flarefin Koi
desc: Fins like a flare going off, trailing light that illuminates nothing around it. Ornamental stock from a garden nobody has placed, on a world nobody has named.

name: Undersea Bee
desc: Thumbnail-sized, barely coherent, and arriving in swarms or not at all. The swarm behaves as one animal, which no single one of them is built to be.

name: Stinkfish
desc: The smell arrives first and outlasts the specimen by days. No compound isolated, no filter effective, and no watch on record has ended in better spirits than it began.

name: Blue Sea Tuna
desc: Big, blue, and built to cross an ocean in a place that has never held one. It makes the crossing anyway, at speed, in whatever direction it happened to be pointed.

name: Rainbow Carp
desc: Ornamental, patterned in colours ship's screens render only approximately. Worth a great deal more to a collector than to a galley, and that is the whole of its value.

name: Blind Crawler
desc: Eyeless, feeling along the bottom of a place that has none, sounding a low note that needs water to make. It makes the note anyway, and does not stop when it is out.

name: Red Snapper
desc: Deep red, sharp-toothed, and a genuine fight from start to finish. One of the few worth recording for its own sake rather than for the tally.

name: Coach
desc: Small, silver, and absolutely everywhere. Named by a rating who found it funnier than the rest of the crew did, and the name went into the manifest before anyone objected.

name: Sufur Diver
desc: Mottled yellow, reeking of sulphur, and inclined to hold position rather than run. It outlasts pursuit rather than outpacing it, which works more often than it should.

name: Storm Salmon
desc: Runs against a current that is not there, hard and in one direction, trailing charge the whole way. What it is running towards has never been established.

name: Shad
desc: Thin silver schooling stock with no school to join. It arrives alone, and conducts itself throughout as though it were among thousands.

name: Silverback
desc: Heavy through the shoulder and silver along the spine, throwing itself clear of a surface that does not exist. A hazard to equipment, and twice now to the crew.

name: Skate
desc: Flat, winged, and gliding on nothing at all. It passes over machinery rather than through it, a distinction the machinery is not equipped to appreciate.

name: Skelleton
desc: A fish with everything except the bones omitted, and misspelled on the first survey sheet and every sheet since. The skeleton was permitted. The rest was not.

name: Spined Loach
desc: Small, whiskered, and armed under the eye with a spine that catches on everything. More trouble than it is worth, and the trade prices it accordingly.

name: Mind Flayer
desc: Jets in a medium with nothing to push against, and moves regardless. Ratings on a long watch beside one report thoughts arriving in their own voice that are not theirs.

name: Crysal Aberration
desc: Faceted and rigid, lit from within in a colour that does not appear on the manifest. Whatever it is aberrating from, the record is clear that it is not going back.

name: Giant Squid
desc: Deep red, long-armed, and inking freely, which becomes a problem when the ink will not stay where it lands. Standard practice is a bucket, and one underneath.

name: Banana Star
desc: Five arms, yellow, curved, and jointed where arms are not jointed. Named by a rating who has since been quietly reassigned. Extremely venomous. Tastes like banana.

name: Crusty Star
desc: Blue, rough as old hull plating, and wholly indifferent to its circumstances. It carries on doing whatever it was doing, at the same rate, throughout.

name: Crystal Star
desc: Rigid, faceted, and ringing faintly whenever it is set down on anything hard. It appears in safety briefings, under the handling section, as the example.

name: Leafy Star
desc: Soft-armed, and regenerating anything taken off it faster than the available material accounts for. What the replacement is made of is a question nobody is funding.

name: Scraggly Star
desc: Thin-armed, uneven, and short one point - and never the same point twice. Reality appears to have made an accounting error here, and elected to let it stand.

name: Ice Tuna
desc: Heavy, cold through, frosted along the flank, and the best eating in the catalogue by a comfortable distance. Worth every bit of the gear it costs to bring one in.

name: Vulcan Cannonfish
desc: Blunt-nosed and barrel-bodied, built to the proportions of ordnance rather than of anything that ever swam. It assumed the shape nearest to hand, and that was the autocannon.

name: Amberjack
desc: Fast, yellow along the tail, and a long fight for an animal of its size. Sought by crews grown tired of logging bass, which is most of them eventually.
